entities.title: A board game is one WebAssembly binary
entities.summary: Each board game is a single .wasm file that carries everything the game needs: its board, pieces, other pictures, its rules text and, later, its rules.
entities.statement: Each board game is a single .wasm file that carries everything the game needs: its board, pieces, other pictures, its rules text and, later, its rules.
entities.rationale: The owner wants a game to be one self-contained binary.
acceptanceCriteria: The table loads a game from one .wasm file and nothing else.
The board, the pieces and the rules text shown to players all come out of that file.
A table keeps playing the exact binary it started with, even after a newer version is published.

origin.description: The owner asked for a plan for a TypeScript web app on icelander.net where friends invited by email play a board game shipped as a WebAssembly binary, with chat, voice chat, a turn indicator, an end-turn button and wins the players acknowledge; the rules come later.

entities.title: Friends are invited by email
entities.summary: A player invites friends to a table by email address; the friend follows the link and signs in with Google to take their seat.
entities.statement: A player invites friends to a table by email address; the friend follows the link and signs in with Google to take their seat.
acceptanceCriteria: Entering an address sends an invitation email with a link to the table.
When mail can't be sent, the inviter is given the link to send themselves.
A friend who signs in with the invited address sees the invitation and can accept or decline it.
Players they have played with before are offered as contacts.

entities.title: Sign in with Google
entities.summary: Players sign in with their Google account through icelander.net's one sign-in, as every game on the site does.
entities.statement: Players sign in with their Google account through icelander.net's one sign-in, as every game on the site does.
acceptanceCriteria: A signed-out visitor is sent to icelander.net's sign-in and comes back to the page they asked for.
The player's name and picture come from their Google account.

entities.title: Chat at the table
entities.summary: Everyone at a table can write messages that everyone else at that table sees at once, and that stay with the game's record.
entities.statement: Everyone at a table can write messages that everyone else at that table sees at once, and that stay with the game's record.
acceptanceCriteria: A message appears for every connected player within a second.
A player who reconnects or joins later sees the chat so far.
Messages are kept in the table's transcript with the time and the sender.

entities.title: Voice chat at the table
entities.summary: Players at a table can talk to each other by voice in the browser, without installing anything.
entities.statement: Players at a table can talk to each other by voice in the browser, without installing anything.
acceptanceCriteria: A player can join and leave the voice chat, and mute themselves.
Everyone shows who is in the voice chat, who is muted and who is speaking.
Voice works between players on ordinary home and mobile networks, including behind NAT.

entities.title: Whose turn it is
entities.summary: The table always shows, to everyone, whose turn it is.
entities.statement: The table always shows, to everyone, whose turn it is.
acceptanceCriteria: Every player sees the same current player, highlighted in the list of seats.
The player whose turn it is is told so clearly (a banner and the tab's title).

entities.title: I'm done with this turn
entities.summary: The player whose turn it is has an "I'm done with this turn" button that passes the turn to the next player.
entities.statement: The player whose turn it is has an "I'm done with this turn" button that passes the turn to the next player.
acceptanceCriteria: Only the player whose turn it is can press it.
Pressing it twice, or on two devices at once, passes the turn once.
The next player is the next seat in the table's order, wrapping round, skipping no one unless the decisions say so.
The transcript records every turn change with its time.

entities.title: Wins count when the players acknowledge them
entities.summary: After a game, a player says who won; the win is recorded only when the other players acknowledge it, which they can do later, after the game.
entities.statement: After a game, a player says who won; the win is recorded only when the other players acknowledge it, which they can do later, after the game.
entities.rationale: The game has no rules yet, so it cannot know who won; the players agree instead.
acceptanceCriteria: Any player at a finished or abandoned table can propose a result: a winner or winners, or no winner.
Each other player can acknowledge or dispute it, during the game or at any time afterwards.
A result counts toward the win record only once the players have acknowledged it as decisions.json "result-consensus" says.
Each player can see their wins per game, and against each friend.

entities.title: Rules come later, without a rewrite
entities.summary: Game rules are not part of the first version, but the design leaves room to add them to the same binary later.
entities.statement: Game rules are not part of the first version, but the design leaves room to add them to the same binary later.
acceptanceCriteria: The first version plays any game as a free table: players move pieces by hand and pass the turn.
The cartridge format has a version number, and adding rules is a new version that old cartridges still load under.
